national_news.title: PM Modi Highlights Spirit of Service During Seva Yatra Interaction
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted virtually with Seva Yatris travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi.
Highlighted key welfare initiatives like PM-KISAN and PM Surya Ghar Yojana for successful last-mile delivery.
Emphasized the vision of building a developed India ('Viksit Bharat') by 2047 with active participation from the youth.

national_news.title: Government Reduces Basic Customs Duty on Crude Edible Oils
bullets: The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution reduced the Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on crude edible oils to curb inflation.
BCD on Crude Sunflower Oil was reduced from 10% to Nil, while Crude Soybean Oil and Crude Palm Oil were reduced from 10% to 5%.
An import duty differential of 19.25% between crude and refined edible oils is maintained, and industry stakeholders are advised to pass full benefits to consumers.

national_news.title: Indian Athletes Shine at Asian Games with Multiple Medals
bullets: Indian runners clinched a silver medal in the mixed 4x400m relay race at the Asian Games in Nagoya.
Seema Kumari won a historic bronze in the women's 10,000m race, marking India's first medal in this event in 16 years.
Roshibina Devi Naorem secured a silver medal in the Women's 60kg Sanda wushu event.

national_news.title: IRDAI Proposes Overhaul of Insurance Distribution Framework
bullets: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposed a three-tier distribution architecture and lower expense limits.
Proposed reforms aim to curb mis-selling, ban volume-linked incentives for bank staff, and enforce commission transparency.
Expense of Management (EoM) limits for life insurers are proposed to be capped at 15% within two years and 12.5% within five years.

national_news.title: Mizoram Launches First 'Pluck & Pay' Festival for Rural Tourism
bullets: Mizoram launched its first 'Pluck & Pay' festival in Khawzawl district at Tualte and Chawngtlai villages to boost rural tourism and direct farm-to-consumer linkages.
The three-day festival (September 23-25) is jointly organized by the state Tourism Department and the Khawzawl Deputy Commissioner's office.
The initiative aims to create direct economic benefits for farming households, homestays, artisans, and local transport operators while showcasing Mizo culture and heritage.

national_news.title: Ministry of Culture to Organize BRICS Theatre Festival 2026
bullets: The Ministry of Culture will organize the BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 from October 12 to 14 in New Delhi under India’s BRICS Presidency.
The festival themed 'Shared Stories, Shared Futures' features participation from nine BRICS member and partner countries including India, Russia, South Africa, and Ethiopia.
The National School of Drama is acting as the nodal agency for organizing this event, building upon the Bhopal Declaration of August 2026.

national_news.title: Indian Railways Approves New Daily Train Service Between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar
bullets: Ministry of Railways approved a new daily overnight train service (Train No. 14153/14154) between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (Terminal).
The service covers a distance of 428 km with a travel time of approximately 8 hours and 10 minutes from Kanpur and 8 hours in the return direction.
The train features eight commercial stoppages including Phaphund, Etawah, Tundla, Hathras, Aligarh, Khurja, Dadri, and Ghaziabad.

national_news.title: FSSAI Proposes Draft Amendment to Restrict 'Paneer' Label Exclusively to Milk-Derived Products
bullets: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) proposed a draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011.
The amendment aims to curb misleading marketing by banning the use of the term 'Paneer' for non-milk-derived or analogue products.
Products licensed under the 'Analogue in Dairy Context' category will be required to discontinue using 'Paneer' in their nomenclature and labelling.

national_news.title: Media Delegation Visits AIIMS Vijaypur and Bahu Fort Aquarium
bullets: A media delegation from Bhopal visited AIIMS Vijaypur in Samba district and the Bahu Fort Aquarium in Jammu under a Press Information Bureau (PIB) exposure tour.
AIIMS Vijaypur has a 750-bed capacity (650 fixed beds), offering 30 broad specialties and 14 super-specialties, and currently admits 125 MBBS students.
The Bahu Fort facility houses India's largest freshwater aquarium, with ongoing Phase-II work featuring North India's first marine aquarium.

bihar_news.title: Finance Ministry Initiates Pre-Budget Meetings for Union Budget 2027-28
bullets: The Union Finance Ministry began a month-long series of pre-budget meetings starting October 12, 2026, to finalize Revised Estimates (RE) for 2026-27 and Budget Estimates (BE) for 2027-28.
The meetings are chaired by the Secretary (Expenditure) and involve discussions with various central ministries and departments.
The upcoming budget is expected to focus on continuing economic reforms, accelerating GDP growth, and generating employment.

bihar_news.title: UP Finance Minister Raises Concerns Over 16th Finance Commission Devolution Formula
bullets: Uttar Pradesh Finance Minister flagged concerns over the 16th Finance Commission's devolution formula for giving higher weight to Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) contribution (increased to 10%) compared to a state's need.

The weight of the income distance criterion was reduced from 45% to 42.5%, which critics argue could adversely affect high-population and fiscally needy states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.
The 16th Finance Commission is headed by Arvind Panagariya, and the central share in divisible tax revenues has been fixed at 41% for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Launches Chief Minister Girl PhD Fellowship Scheme
bullets: The Bihar Government announced the Chief Minister Girl PhD Fellowship Scheme to promote higher education and research among female students.
Under the scheme, 1,000 selected female doctoral researchers will receive a monthly fellowship of ₹10,000 for a duration of four years.
Each beneficiary will receive a total financial assistance of ₹4.8 lakh to reduce financial barriers and boost women's participation in research careers.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves New Sugar Mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada District
bullets: The Bihar Cabinet approved a proposal to set up a new sugar mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada district, bringing an investment of over ₹500 crore.
The project spans around 102 acres at Makanpur and aims to benefit sugarcane growers across Nawada, Nalanda, Sheikhpura, and Jamui districts.
The original historic mill (Mohini Sugar Works) was established in 1952 and shut down in 1993; the new initiative aims to revive industrial activity and create local employment.

bihar_news.title: Bihar CM Directs Long-Term Kosi Flood Management Strategy and Major Infrastructure Projects
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary directed officials to develop a long-term flood mitigation strategy for the Kosi river system, focusing on silt management and a new barrage.
Reviewed major projects including the 348 km Buxar-Bhagalpur 6-lane Greenfield Expressway, Ganga-Ambika Path, and the 2400 MW (3x800 MW) Pirpainti Thermal Power Project.
Emphasized accelerating the PM-KUSUM scheme to solarise agricultural feeders and operate state-owned tubewells using solar energy.

bihar_news.title: CJI Surya Kant to Inaugurate India's First Victim Rights Centre at Patna
bullets: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant will inaugurate the Victim Rights Centre at the Bihar State Legal Services Authority (BSLSA) in Patna on September 26, 2026.
Established as a pilot project under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, functioning as a single-window system for crime victims.
The initiative integrates support from multiple legal, medical, and welfare schemes such as the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and Bihar Victim Compensation Scheme, 2014.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Introduces State Subsidy Top-Up for Rooftop Solar under PM Surya Ghar Yojana
bullets: Bihar introduced additional state incentives under the Mukhyamantri Solar Protsahan Yojana to supplement the central PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.
Combined central and state subsidies provide up to ₹98,000 for a 3 kW rooftop solar system in the state.
The initiative aims to reduce upfront installation costs and accelerate decentralised renewable energy adoption across residential households.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy 2026
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister reviewed the draft Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy 2026, aiming to attract around ₹16,000 crore in investments and generate 12,000 jobs.
The policy focuses on promoting green hydrogen production, utilisation, and supporting infrastructure within the state.
It is aligned with the National Green Hydrogen Mission's 2030 targets of achieving 5 million metric tonnes of annual green hydrogen production.
